title: Making a massive-scale RTS. Still a lot of work, even with AI.
author: purri-cat-studio
selftext:
Love RTS games. Hate how they never feel grand. What if we had a  huge map with towns and cities that we could zoom down in and watch the combat? Needs plenty of explosions and nukes of course.   


Out of that concept was born [There Is Eternal War](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5193960/There_Is_Eternal_War/) whose lore came out of a thought experiment I did awhile ago where I tried to build a grim-dark universe where every faction was equally evil (Yes Chaos in 40k is clearly more evil than the Imperium)

I'm quite pleased with how it's turning out. You don't control individual units. Instead you plan out divisions with desired unit compositions and then assign factories and barracks to pump out the forces for them. 

Basebuilding has to be clustered around town centers and there is a limit to how many buildings fit around these TCs which results in city-like complexes spread out around the map. 

AI was very helpful in doing all the tedious coding with me directing which allowed me to spend more time on the art, all 2D sprites btw.

In fact the AI was really, really, great at optimizing. I can get 20,000 or more units active on my 14 year old laptop screen and maintain 50fps. I'd never have been able to do so much all on my own.

How are you simulating tons of units? I am struggling massively with this myself even after optimization passes where running 3 AI vs a Player can make the game chug because so many nodes exist and are pathing etc.

Looks very cool!

replies.author: purri-cat-studio
replies.body:
I enjoy talking about this so I'll go into detail:

\- sprites are all billboards using Godots multi-mesh to optimize rendering. They have 8-directional animations and the shadows is just another multimesh rendered underneath them.   
\- Divisional level decision making. A big part of the game mechanics is the division system where players create divisions, set out the type and number of units they want to be in the division and then assign barracks to produce units for the division. This means that I can then delegate most thinking to the division and not each unit. The division will handle finding a path which all the units in the division then take, and also scans for targets using whatever units are alive in the division, and so on. This means individual units are as dumb as possible and we reduce the number of thinking required in the game.

On the rendering side there is a lot you can do to optimize.   
\- fog of war  
\- reducing particle effects. I use sprite effects wherever possible.  
\- turning off particle effects and lights when not visible
